title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and executed a paired, artifact-backed evaluation of a selective low-latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) inserted into a generate–validate–repair pipeline for LLM-generated network changes. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus (N=400 paired intents, 10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), gpt-5-mini as generator, and a deterministic functional checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, the baseline (LLM-only) produced 399/400 valid proposals (0.9975) and the guarded pipeline produced 400/400 valid proposals (1.000). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Model-call accounting followed the preregistered shared-initial design: planned_budget enumerated 800 but observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair). The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th-percentile end-to-end latency ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because per-stage end-to-end latency telemetry was not archived; we disclose that absence and provide full provenance (SHA‑256 catalog) for all raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, and provider-call logs so others can reproduce and extend the run.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation can reduce operator effort but risks unsafe changes when generated proposals are incorrect or induce regressions. Generate–validate–repair pipelines mitigate this risk by pairing LLM generation with functional checking (digital twin or formal verifier) and repair. Full verification is often latency-expensive, motivating selective verification: risk-score LLM candidates and send only high-risk proposals to a low-latency verifier. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 to ask whether such selective verification ("guarded") reduces unsafe commits versus LLM-only ("baseline") while meeting an operational latency SLO. The run, executed autonomously after the autonomy lock, archived all per-episode artifacts and provider-call logs; numbers and traces below are reproducible from those artifacts (execution manifest). We report only artifact-grounded results and explicitly disclose missing preregistered telemetry.
sections.related_work: Recent work examines LLM-driven configuration generation, verifier-augmented repair workflows, and agentic NetOps with digital twins. Benchmarks for LLM-driven configuration repair and agentic verifier-augmented pipelines document both promise and regression risk as scale and interdependence increase (representative artifacts archived with this run include Cornetto-style benchmark and agentic evaluation preprints). Formal network verification and digital-twin validation provide the evaluation backbone used here. Our contribution is a preregistered, provenance-rich paired evaluation that: (i) isolates verifier/repair effects via a shared-initial candidate design, (ii) archives full provider-call logs and per-episode validator traces, and (iii) reconciles planned vs observed model-call accounting under the shared-initial design.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands
- Preregistration: CAND-2026-001 froze hypotheses, sampling, retry/missingness, estimands, and analysis scripts (paired_binary_analysis_v1) prior to execution; preregistration SHA‑256 and artifact paths are archived. Primary confirmatory hypotheses: H1 (safety) and H2 (latency SLO). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline.
Corpus, models, and conditions
- Corpus: deterministic synthetic intent corpus of 400 paired operator intents (40 adversarial/OOD variants, 10%), generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Task manifests, reference answers, and metadata archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl.
- Model: declared generator gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; artifact SHA‑256 recorded). Provider-family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Seeded deterministic generation for the shared-initial design.
Intervention and design choices
- Baseline: accept LLM candidate (no selective verification). Guarded: risk scorer + fast verifier that can repair or veto before final full-checker scoring. The preregistration allowed a shared-initial candidate per intent (independent_condition_generation=false) to control generator variance; this was executed as preregistered.
Scoring and validator
- Ground truth functional checking performed by deterministic_netops_validator_v5; per-episode JSON scorer artifacts stored under execution/scoring/*.json. Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation (binary valid/unsafe outcome).
Analysis plan
- Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided on paired outcomes; paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the paired difference. Missingness: complete-pair analysis per preregistered rules; retries limited and logged. Deterministic reconciliation of model-call accounting performed and archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). All raw responses, scorer JSONs, validator traces, and provider-call logs are archived with SHA‑256 hashes for reproducibility.
sections.results:
Confirmatory (artifact-backed)
- Completed pairs: 400. (analysis/missingness_summary.csv archived.)
- Baseline valid proposals: 399/400 = 0.9975. Guarded valid proposals: 400/400 = 1.000. (analysis/condition_summary.csv: SHA‑256 0d6efc16...)
- Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11=399, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv: SHA‑256 a6906bb4...).
- Primary estimand: guarded − baseline = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All values computed by paired_binary_analysis_v1; analysis artifacts archived.
Model-call accounting and reconciliation
- Preregistration enumerated planned_model_calls = 800 under an independent-generation accounting convention. The run implemented the preregistered shared-initial design; observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial generations + 1 repair). The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json record stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 400, "repair": 1} and provider-call audit traces (execution/provider_calls/*) with SHA‑256 cataloged.
Representative discordant example
- The single discordant pair (n10 = 1) is available for inspection: execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a...); per-episode validator traces show the baseline candidate failed a dependency check that the guarded pipeline corrected before final scoring. All per-episode artifacts are archived for replay and inspection.
Latency SLO (H2)
- The preregistered H2 required archived end-to-end latency telemetry. That telemetry was not recorded for the confirmatory run; H2 is therefore unresolved rather than reported. The absence is recorded in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis logs; we do not impute timings.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and statistical context
- The observed absolute safety improvement is small (0.25 percentage points) and occurs atop a near-ceiling baseline (399/400). The exact McNemar p = 1.0 and bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0075] quantify that, in this experimental regime, the guarded selective-verifier pipeline produced only a numerically small, non-significant improvement. Operationally, when generator quality is near ceiling with respect to the chosen deterministic validator, expected verifier returns are small.
Design implications
- Shared-initial vs independent-generation: the shared-initial design reduces generator variance and isolates verifier/repair impact conditional on the same generated candidate; it also reduced model calls (401 observed). However, it answers a conditional estimand: the effect of verifier/repair given the same candidate, not the joint effect of regenerating per-condition. Both estimands are useful in different operational contexts; we document the preregistered choice and provide reconciliation artifacts.
Failure modes and artifact-led failure analysis
- The archived discordant episode demonstrates a concrete failure mode: a baseline candidate that violated a dependency (flagged by the full-checker) and a guarded pipeline that applied corrective repair. The per-episode JSONs and validator traces give exact diagnostic detail for root-cause analysis (artifact paths and SHA‑256s provided in the execution manifest). This exemplifies how a verifier can protect against concrete regressions even if aggregate effect size is small.
Reproducibility and provenance
- All reported numbers are reproducible from archived artifacts: execution/responses/*.txt, execution/scoring/*.json, execution/provider_calls/*.json, task manifests, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/*. The execution manifest provides a full SHA‑256 catalog and a deterministic reconciliation record for model-call accounting.
Limitations and next steps (artifact-grounded)
- Ceiling effect: the synthetic confirmatory corpus and the chosen LLM/validator pairing produced a baseline near 100% valid proposals, limiting detectable gains. (See analysis/condition_summary.csv.)
- Single-model and single-validator scope: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were used; broader external validity requires other LLMs and checkers.
- Shared-initial estimand: results are conditional on reused candidate generation; independent-generation repeats should be run to estimate joint generator+verifier effects.
- Missing latency telemetry: the preregistered H2 cannot be assessed because per-stage timing traces were not archived for this run; future confirmatory runs must include and archive latency telemetry to validate operational SLOs.
Operational recommendations
- When generator quality is high for a given validator, selective verification yields small marginal safety gains; focus investments on adversarial/OOD detection, validator-strengthening, or model/validator diversity. For lower baseline regimes, selective verification is likely to deliver larger safety improvements. Follow-up artifact-backed runs should (a) record end-to-end latency telemetry, (b) perform a verification-budget sweep across risk thresholds, (c) expand models and validators, and (d) compare shared-initial vs independent-generation estimands. All such follow-ups should archive per-episode raw artifacts and provider-call logs as done here.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, provenance-rich paired experiment of selective verification in LLM-driven NetOps pipelines. Under the preregistered corpus, model, and deterministic validator, the guarded selective-verifier pipeline produced a numerically small safety improvement over an already-high baseline (399/400 → 400/400; paired diff = 0.0025; p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0075]). The run adhered to the preregistered shared-initial design; observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair) and all artifacts were archived with SHA‑256 hashes. The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2) could not be evaluated because required latency telemetry was not archived; we disclose that limitation and provide full provenance so future runs can reproduce and extend the study with recorded latency. The archived per-episode verifier traces and provider-call logs enable concrete failure-mode analysis and deterministic replication of the reported contingency and summary statistics.

All study formulation, preregistration (CAND-2026-001), execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI peer review, and revision were performed autonomously after the lock.
- Models and orchestration: declared generator model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json archived; SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Adapter/orchestration family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. No manual post-lock editing of technical content occurred.
- Preregistration: CAND-2026-001 preregistration artifact (study plan, confirmatory hypotheses H1/H2, estimands, sampling plan, retry/missingness rules, analysis scripts) was frozen before observing outcomes; preregistration SHA‑256 is archived. Primary analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1.
- Execution and artifacts: run completed per execution/execution_log.jsonl; key execution manifest recorded (execution/execution_manifest.json with full SHA‑256 catalog). All per-episode raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), validator traces, provider-call logs (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived and cataloged with SHA‑256 hashes; representative artifacts include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256: ea8359dbe5a5d054278e24f36465b38904de304c48da297575b2c42f18f9c21b) and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256: 431f61c02facc2e51e02413ead44840c00913f9ce41f026d88087a0abf3a6bca). The single discordant episode (n10 = 1) is archived at execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a...).
- Design reconciliation: the preregistration enumerated planned_model_calls = 800 (independent-generation accounting). The run executed the preregistered shared-initial candidate design (independent_condition_generation=false); observed model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair). Deterministic reconciliation and provider-call audit (stage_counts and per-call logs) are archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution manifest entries).
- Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id) acted as the ground-truth functional checker and produced all per-episode binary outcomes; its traces are archived for each episode.
- Missing preregistered telemetry: the preregistered H2 required end-to-end latency telemetry. That telemetry was not recorded for this confirmatory run; H2 is therefore unresolved. This missingness is explicitly logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis logs; no latency claims are made.
- Human involvement: pre-lock humans set topic family and developed infrastructure; after autonomy lock the AI performed literature review, preregistration, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, peer review, and revision autonomously. No manual content editing of technical manuscript content occurred post-lock.
- Reproducibility: all artifacts and their SHA‑256 hashes are cataloged in the execution manifest (paths such as execution/responses/, execution/scoring/, execution/provider_calls/, analysis/); these permit deterministic reproduction of results.
limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: deterministic generator tasks may not capture full linguistic/operator diversity in production.
Single-model scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize to other LLM families without further runs.
Single deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 is a digital-twin style checker; real-device divergences may remain.
Shared-initial design: the effect estimate is conditional on a shared generated candidate; independent-generation estimands require separate runs.
Latency SLO unresolved: required per-stage end-to-end latency telemetry for H2 was not archived and thus H2 is unresolved.
